decision_rule: Spearman(fidelity, harden_gap) < -0.3 with one-sided p < 0.05 across the 10 instances -> the scaffold-fidelity rule TRANSFERS to heterogeneous instances. Otherwise it does not transfer (null preserved as a finding). Win/loss head-to-head (harden vs rigid per instance) reported descriptively; it is not the decision criterion.
fidelity_measure: Frozen from when-hardening-helps A12/C13/C17: scaffold = pairwise centroid-distance ordering at compress-end (last 'compress' frame) of the best-L harden run; reference = best-known optimum arrangement (lowest L across both methods and all seeds); fidelity = Spearman rho between the two distance orderings; harden_gap = best harden L - best-known L.
hypothesis: The scaffold-fidelity rule transfers: across heterogeneous rectangle instances, higher scaffold fidelity (Spearman correlation of compress-end pairwise centroid distances vs the best-known optimum arrangement) predicts a smaller gap between hardening's best result and the best-known optimum.
instance_notes: Uniform instances use engine genPieces({n, w:[lo,hi], h:[lo,hi]}, pseed). Bimodal instances compose genPieces({n: n_large, w: large, h: large}, pseed) ++ genPieces({n: n_small, w: small, h: small}, pseed+1000); large pieces listed first. All instance generation is deterministic given pseed.
question: When pieces vary in size, does the disk scaffold's arrangement still predict hardening's outcome (the scaffold-fidelity rule from when-hardening-helps)?
title: Does the scaffold-fidelity rule transfer to heterogeneous instances?
